title: Delete user-owned custom emoji on account deletion
owner_decision: Delete user data and owned files after the account-deletion database commit; retain household chat messages with anonymized authors.
classification: Confirmed by source inspection: deleting an uploader nulled CustomEmoji.uploaded_by_user_id but retained the user-uploaded emoji row and file.

change.database: Account deletion explicitly removes custom emoji rows uploaded by that account.
change.files: The existing managed cleanup queue captures valid chat-emoji filenames before deletion and purges them after commit. Files still referenced by another row are preserved.

verification.result: passed: 6 tests on Python 3.14.10 and PostgreSQL 17.6
verification.coverage: The deletion regression verifies the uploaded emoji row and file are removed, alongside avatar/thumbnail, chat attachment, save and history cleanup, while household chat messages remain with an anonymous author. FK inventory matches the fresh migrated schema.
verification.database: Fresh oneirodexemoji_test database upgraded from Alembic baseline through head; dropped after verification. TEST_DATABASE_URL was process-scoped; root .env unchanged.

limits: The test covers immediate post-commit emoji file cleanup; it does not inject an emoji-specific unlink failure. The generic retry worker was separately exercised in R1978.
Other retained user-authored fields still require classification, and the deployed operator schema has not been compared.
